macros.description: A dictionary of string substitutions. Global macros can be used in any configuration value; model macros are scoped to their model. Macro names must be <64 chars, match ^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$, and not be PID, PORT, or MODEL_ID. Values can be string, number, or boolean. Macros can reference other macros defined before them.

connect.description: TCP connection timeout in seconds. Set to 0 to disable.

keepalive.description: TCP keepalive timeout in seconds. Set to 0 to disable.

responseHeader.description: Time to wait for response headers in seconds. Set to 0 to disable.

tlsHandshake.description: TLS handshake timeout in seconds. Set to 0 to disable.

expectContinue.description: Expect-Continue timeout in seconds. Set to 0 to disable.

idleConn.description: Idle connection timeout in seconds. Set to 0 to disable.

swap.description: Controls model swapping behaviour within the group. True: only one model runs at a time. False: all models can run together.

exclusive.description: Controls how the group affects other groups. True: causes all other groups to unload when this group runs a model. False: does not affect other groups.

persistent.description: Prevents other groups from unloading the models in this group. Does not affect individual model behaviour.

members.description: Array of model IDs that are members of this group. Model IDs must be defined in models.

groupsConfig.description: A dictionary of group settings. Provides advanced controls over model swapping behaviour. Model IDs must be defined in models. A model can only be a member of one group. Behaviour controlled via swap, exclusive, persistent.

matrixConfig.description: Solver-based alternative to groups. Declares valid combinations of concurrent models. The solver minimizes eviction cost when swapping. A config must use either groups or matrix, not both.

vars.description: Short names for models. Keys must be alphanumeric, 1-8 characters. All sets and evict_costs must use these IDs.

evict_costs.description: Relative cost of evicting a running model. Models not listed default to 1. Values must be positive integers.

sets.description: Named sets of concurrent model combinations. Values are DSL strings using & (AND), | (OR), () (grouping), and +ref (inline another set). Definition order is used for tie-breaking.

healthCheckTimeout.description: Number of seconds to wait for a model to be ready to serve requests.

globalTTL.description: Default TTL for all models in seconds, 0 means no TTL and models will never be automatically unloaded

unloadTimeout.description: Graceful timeout in seconds when unloading a model (manual, API, or TTL expiry) before force-killing the model process. 0 uses the default of 10 seconds.

globalConcurrencyLimit.description: Caps the number of inference requests served at once across all models combined, using a single shared semaphore rather than a per-model limit. 0 means no limit. Requests exceeding the limit receive an HTTP 429 Too Many Requests response immediately rather than being queued.

logLevel.description: Sets the logging value. Valid values: debug, info, warn, error.

logTimeFormat.description: Enables and sets the logging timestamp format. Valid values: "", "ansic", "unixdate", "rubydate", "rfc822", "rfc822z", "rfc850", "rfc1123", "rfc1123z", "rfc3339", "rfc3339nano", "kitchen", "stamp", "stampmilli", "stampmicro", and "stampnano". For more info, read: https://pkg.go.dev/time#pkg-constants

metricsMaxInMemory.description: Maximum number of metrics to keep in memory. Controls how many metrics are stored before older ones are discarded.

captureBuffer.description: Size in megabytes of the buffer for storing request/response captures. Set to 0 to disable captures.

path.description: SQLite database file path for persistent activity logs.

store.description: Store configuration for durable llama-swap state.

audit.description: Conversation audit settings. Conversations live in a dedicated audit store next to the operational database: rows in audit/audit.db, bodies as zstd-compressed content-addressed blocks in audit/segments. maxBytes bounds the compressed on-disk audit size.

retention.description: Conversation retention; seconds or a duration such as 720h.

maxBytes.description: Compressed on-disk budget for the audit store in bytes.

storeMedia.description: Inline uploaded media file content in the structured capture.

activityRetention.description: Retention for operational activity rows; seconds or a duration. Independent of conversation retention; 0 keeps them indefinitely.

session_id.description: Ordered request headers used to identify sessions in the Activity page.

every.description: Delay between polling for new performance statistics. Minimum duration is 1s. Lower values use more RAM as stats are kept in memory.

performance.description: Configuration for CPU, RAM and GPU monitoring statistics.

disabled.description: Disable power monitoring and energy statistics.

electricityPricePerKwh.description: Base electricity price per kWh in the configured currency. With no tariffs every sample is priced with it; otherwise it prices the time no tariff window covers.

currency.description: Currency label shown with cost figures, e.g. CNY or USD.

name.description: Time-of-use window label, e.g. peak or valley.

pricePerKwh.description: Price per kWh while this window is active.

start.description: Window start in HH:MM local time.

end.description: Window end in HH:MM local time. Earlier than start wraps across midnight. Windows must not overlap.

tariffs.description: Optional time-of-use electricity price windows. Times not covered by any window use electricityPricePerKwh.

retentionDays.description: How many days of power samples and occupancy intervals to keep.

flushInterval.description: How often sampled power is aggregated and written to the store. Minimum duration is 15s.

disabled.description: Disable the node-level IPMI power collector.

command.description: Path to the ipmitool binary. Empty uses the ipmitool found on PATH.

ipmi.description: Node-level power via local ipmitool (DCMI preferred, sensor readings as fallback). When unavailable the panel falls back to GPU power only.

stopC.description: GPU core temperature in Celsius at which every model occupying the card is stopped and parked in maintenance mode. Required when thermalGuard is set; sane values are 80-90.

resumeC.description: Temperature at which parked models leave maintenance again. Defaults to stopC minus 5. Must be lower than stopC.

consecutive.description: Consecutive hot samples required before acting; each sample is one performance.every tick, so a transient sensor spike does not unload serving models.

failover.description: Forward requests for thermally parked models to configured providers (gateway) or peers instead of answering 503.

thermalGuard.description: Overheat protection: when a GPU crosses stopC its models are stopped and parked in maintenance until the card cools below resumeC. Requests fail over to providers/peers when configured.

power.description: GPU and node power monitoring, energy statistics and electricity cost accounting.

startPort.description: Starting port number for the automatic ${PORT} macro. The ${PORT} macro is incremented for every model that uses it. Ports are handed out by model ID order, so adding or removing a model can move the ports of models that sort after it; that move is not treated as a configuration change for them.

sendLoadingState.description: Inject loading status updates into the reasoning field. When true, a stream of loading messages will be sent to the client.

includeAliasesInList.description: Present aliases within the /v1/models OpenAI API listing. when true, model aliases will be output to the API model listing duplicating all fields except for Id so chat UIs can use the alias equivalent to the original.

profiles.description: Runtime-selectable model ID rewrites. One profile or none may be active at runtime.

pins.description: Model IDs to rewrite while this profile is active. Targets may be concrete models, aliases, peer models, or selector IDs. An empty string or null disables the model ID.

selectors.description: Virtual model IDs that select a concrete target for each request. Selectors run after profiles and are not supported on /upstream paths.

strategy.description: How a target is selected for each request.

targets.description: Ordered target model IDs or aliases. Selector IDs cannot be targets.

spillover.description: Requests reserved per active target before spilling over to the next target.

name.description: Display name used in the /v1/models response.

unlisted.description: Hide this selector from /v1/models while keeping it requestable.

models.description: A dictionary of model configurations. Each key is a model's ID. Model settings have defaults if not defined. The model's ID is available as ${MODEL_ID}.

cmd.description: Command to run to start the inference server. Macros can be used. Comments allowed with |.

cmdStop.description: Command to run to stop the model gracefully. Uses ${PID} macro for upstream process id. If empty, default shutdown behavior is used.

name.description: Display name for the model. Used in v1/models API response.

description.description: Description for the model. Used in v1/models API response.

env.description: Array of environment variables to inject into cmd's environment. Each value is a string in ENV_NAME=value format.

proxy.description: URL where llama-swap routes API requests. If custom port is used in cmd, this must be set.

aliases.description: Alternative model names for this configuration. Must be unique globally.

checkEndpoint.description: URL path to check if the server is ready. Use 'none' to skip health checking.

ttl.description: Automatically unload the model after ttl seconds. -1 uses the global TTL value, 0 disables unloading. Must be >0 to enable.

unloadTimeout.description: Graceful timeout in seconds when unloading this model (manual, API, or TTL expiry) before force-killing it. 0 uses the global unloadTimeout.

useModelName.description: Override the model name sent to upstream server. Useful if upstream expects a different name.

stripParams.description: Comma separated list of parameters to remove from the request. Used for server-side enforcement of sampling parameters.

setParams.description: Dictionary of parameters to set/override in requests. Useful for enforcing specific parameter values. Protected params like 'model' cannot be overridden. Values can be strings, numbers, booleans, arrays, or objects.

setParamsByID.description: Dictionary mapping requested model IDs (or aliases) to parameters to set/override in requests. Applied after setParams and can override those values. Useful with aliases to vary behaviour depending on which alias the client used (e.g. different reasoning_effort per alias). Keys support ${MODEL_ID} macro substitution. Protected params like 'model' cannot be overridden.

filters.description: Dictionary of filter settings. Supports stripParams, setParams, and setParamsByID.

metadata.description: Dictionary of arbitrary values included in /v1/models. Can contain complex types. Only passed through in /v1/models responses.

concurrencyLimit.description: Overrides allowed number of active parallel requests to a model. 0 uses internal default of 10. >0 overrides default. Requests exceeding limit get HTTP 429.

sendLoadingState.description: Overrides the global sendLoadingState for this model. Ommitting this property will use the global setting.

unlisted.description: If true the model will not show up in /v1/models responses. It can still be used as normal in API requests.

disableKeepAlives.description: Open a new upstream connection for every request instead of reusing idle ones. Works around upstreams that close a connection they advertised as keep-alive, such as llama-server after a streamed response (#1205). When true, timeouts.idleConn has no effect.

ignoreWebsockets.description: Do not let websocket connections load a stopped model or count toward concurrency, TTL activity, swap decisions, selector load, or in-flight activity.

in.description: List of input modalities understood by the model.

out.description: List of output modalities generated by the model.

tools.description: Whether the model supports function calling.

reranker.description: Whether the model supports the /v1/rerank endpoint.

context.description: Maximum token context length supported by the model.

translation.description: Marks the model as a translation model (for example Hy-MT2). Clients use it to group the model under translation tooling.

voices.description: Voice IDs returned by GET /v1/audio/voices for this model without asking the upstream. The endpoint is non-standard and upstream answers are unreliable, so set this when a speech model ships a fixed voice list. Never rendered into /v1/models.

disableAuto.description: Disable automatic capability discovery for this model. By default llama-swap asks the upstream server what it supports when the model becomes ready and fills in any capability left unset here.

capabilities.description: Defines what the model accepts for input, output and other metadata. Used in v1/models to inform clients what the model can do. An empty capabilities block (all zero values) is treated as not configured.

backend.description: Structured backend definition. Remove cmd when using this shape; the legacy cmd path remains fully compatible and takes precedence when both are present.

runtime.description: Name of a managed runtime that provides this backend, instead of a system binary.

runtimeVersion.description: Pin the model to one installed version of backend.runtime. Requires runtime.

protocol.description: Upstream protocol adaptation applied by llama-swap.

apis.description: API families this backend serves. Limits which proxy routes are bound to it.

discover.description: Discover the process port from the runtime instead of expecting llama-swap to set one.

args.description: Structured argv. Used when cmd is absent; ${PORT} and macros are expanded.

mode.description: process keeps a resident process; sleep lets llama-swap park it.

sleepLevel.description: How deeply to park a sleeping backend.

gpuAffinity.description: GPU card ids this model may occupy.

priority.description: Scheduling priority for this model's runtime. Higher wins when the budget is contended.

evictionPriority.description: Order in which runtimes are evicted when the budget is exceeded. Lower is evicted first.

container.description: Run the backend inside a container managed by llama-swap.

mounts.description: Host paths exposed inside the container.

stopTimeout.description: Grace period before SIGKILL, in seconds or as a duration such as 10s.

launch.description: Legacy structured launch settings. Values are folded into backend.args when the configuration loads (the command text is the single source of truth), so newly saved models never contain this block.

model.description: Model path or name to serve.

servedModelName.description: Name the upstream engine serves this model as.

contextPerRequest.description: Per-request context limit, overriding the engine default.

maxConcurrency.description: Maximum concurrent requests inside the engine.

gpus.description: GPU cards the engine may use.

tensorParallelSize.description: Number of GPUs a single engine is sharded across.

pricing.description: Attach this model to a pricing catalog entry so the usage records page can estimate its cost.

model.description: Model name in the pricing catalog.

lmcache.description: Attach a vLLM backend to LMCache. Only supported for vllm backends with a managed runtime.

mode.description: mp runs a standalone LMCache server; inProcess keeps the built-in connector.

host.description: ZMQ server host for the mp mode.

port.description: ZMQ server port for the mp mode.

chunkSize.description: KV chunk size for the inProcess mode. 0 keeps the library default.

entrypoint.description: Optional custom launch head for a native managed runtime (for example "python3 /scripts/server.py"). It runs verbatim under the runtime's environment, followed by args; no engine flags, host or port are injected.

preload.description: List of model IDs to load on startup. Model names must match keys in models. When preloading multiple models, define a group to prevent swapping.

profile.description: Profile to activate on startup and after a configuration reload. Must name a key under profiles. An empty value starts with no profile active.

hooks.description: A dictionary of event triggers and actions. Only supported hook is on_startup.

logToStdout.description: Controls what is logged to stdout. 'proxy': logs generated by llama-swap, 'upstream': copy of upstream process stdout logs, 'both': both interleaved together, 'none': no logs written to stdout.

id.description: Stable identifier for the key. Derived from the secret when omitted.

name.description: Human readable label shown in the control plane.

key.description: The secret itself. Also accepted as value or secret.

scopes.description: Scopes granted to the key. Defaults to inference only.

models.description: Model IDs the key may call. Empty means every model.

apiKeys.description: Require an API key when making requests to inference endpoints. When empty, authorization will not be checked. Each entry is either a non-empty string (full legacy admin) or an object with key/name/scopes/models. Secrets are hashed into the SQLite store at startup.

proxy.description: A valid base URL to proxy requests to. Requested path to llama-swap will be appended to the end of the proxy value.

apiKey.description: A string key to be injected into the request. If blank, no key will be added. Key will be injected into headers: Authorization: Bearer <key> and x-api-key: <key>.

models.description: A list of models served by the peer.

stripParams.description: Comma separated list of parameters to remove from the request. Useful for removing parameters that the peer doesn't support.

setParams.description: Dictionary of parameters to set/override in requests to this peer. Useful for injecting provider-specific settings. Protected params like 'model' cannot be overridden. Values can be strings, numbers, booleans, arrays, or objects.

filters.description: Dictionary of filter settings for peer requests. Supports stripParams and setParams.

keepalive.description: TCP keepalive connection timeout in seconds.

responseHeader.description: Time to wait for response headers in seconds.

timeouts.description: Timeout settings for proxy connections to this peer.

peers.description: A dictionary of remote peers and models they provide. Peers can be another llama-swap or any server that provides the /v1/ generative API endpoints supported by llama-swap.

type.description: Upstream API protocol of the single-adapter shorthand. openai injects Authorization: Bearer; openai-responses speaks /v1/responses; anthropic injects x-api-key and anthropic-version headers; gemini injects x-goog-api-key and serves /v1beta/models/{model}:generateContent paths; gemini-interactions serves /v1beta/interactions (Steps in, an Interaction with steps[] and modality usage out). Must be empty when adapters are configured.

endpoint.description: Base URL of the single-adapter shorthand, e.g. https://api.deepseek.com. Request paths are appended to it. Must be empty when adapters are configured.

proxy.description: Provider-level outbound proxy (http/https/socks5/socks5h URL, or the literal 'direct' to bypass environment proxies). Key-level proxy overrides this; empty inherits environment proxies.

priority.description: Default priority inherited by keys without their own. Higher priority tiers are used first.

weight.description: Default weighted-round-robin weight inherited by keys without their own. Zero weights share equally.

sticky.description: Enable session affinity: requests from one conversation stick to the same provider API surface (provider + adapter + key), because a provider's surfaces keep separate upstream prompt caches. One conversation keeps its cache; different conversations still spread across the pool.

exposeUpstreamName.description: Keep the upstream model name callable next to the local name and its aliases. Default true: a client may use an alias or the name the vendor itself uses, so renaming a model never takes the vendor name away. Set false to publish only the names this provider declares.

bareNamePolicy.description: Arbitration for the bare model name when a local configured model shares it. local-first keeps local precedence; provider-first lets this provider win.

maxRetries.description: How many times one key may be retried before it is benched and the request continues on the next key. 0 tries each key once. Only transient failures (5xx, network errors, truncated streams) consume the budget; 401/402/429 bench the key immediately because retrying them cannot help.

disabled.description: Manually disable this provider. Disabled providers do not serve requests and are excluded from /v1/models.

sessionHeaders.description: Request headers set to the session id on upstream requests. The caller's session id (the first non-empty header listed in ui.activity.session_id) is passed through when present; otherwise a value derived from the conversation prefix is used.

headers.description: Static request headers sent upstream. Credential headers (Authorization, x-api-key, x-goog-api-key) and session headers are managed by the gateway and cannot be set here.

adapters.description: Upstream API surfaces of one provider. Each adapter carries its own dialect, endpoint and model list; configure several for a subscription that exposes multiple APIs (e.g. OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic and Google surfaces of one plan). When set, the top-level type/endpoint/models must be empty.

name.description: Optional label used by the UI and in error messages, e.g. "Chat" or "Google".

type.description: The upstream API surface: openai (Completions, /v1/chat/completions), openai-responses (/v1/responses), anthropic (/v1/messages) or gemini (/v1beta/models/...). It decides both the auth header style and the request dialect; a client speaking another dialect is converted into this one before forwarding.

endpoint.description: Base URL of this adapter. Request paths are appended to it.

proxy.description: Outbound proxy for this adapter: http/https/socks5/socks5h URL, or the literal 'direct' to bypass all proxies. Overrides the credential and provider level; a model-level proxy overrides this one.

pathMap.description: Literal request-path prefix rewrites applied before forwarding; the longest matching prefix wins. Example: {"/v1beta/models/": "/v1/models/"} for an upstream that serves the Gemini dialect under /v1.

modelMatch.description: Glob patterns (e.g. "grok-*") used to route models pulled from a template's model list into this adapter.

default.description: Marks the catch-all adapter for pulled models that match no other adapter's modelMatch patterns. At most one adapter may set it.

apiKeys.description: Optional credential override for this adapter; empty inherits the provider apiKeys.

value.description: The API key value. Omitted from config JSON output.

valueEnv.description: Environment variable holding the key value.

models.description: Models served by this adapter (local -> upstream name).

aliases.description: Extra client-facing names for the same upstream model. They route (and satisfy access-key allowlists) exactly like local, but are not listed separately in /v1/models.

proxy.description: Outbound proxy for this model only: http/https/socks5/socks5h URL, or the literal 'direct'. The most specific level; empty inherits the adapter, then the credential, then the provider, then the global network proxy.

capabilities.description: What the upstream model accepts and produces. The playground files provider models by it: in/out modalities decide chat, image, speech and transcription tooling (text->image is image generation), translation marks a translation model.

pricing.description: Pin the pricing-catalog entry used to estimate this model's cost. Empty parts resolve from the provider (its pricingProvider, else its own id lowercased) and the upstream model name.

provider.description: Provider id in the pricing catalog.

model.description: Model name in the pricing catalog.

cooldown.description: Per-provider cooldown policy: "inherit" (default) uses the gateway-wide settings, "enabled" keeps cooldowns (optionally with this provider's own durations), "disabled" never benches this provider's credentials (failures are still recorded and requests still fail over).

auth.description: Override the auth cooldown (Go duration), e.g. 30s.

authProbe.description: Override how long the first 401 benches a key (Go duration, 0s disables probing).

modelPrefix.description: Prefix prepended to every model name this provider exposes in /v1/models and for routing (e.g. "go-" turns glm-5.1 into go-glm-5.1). Empty (the default) exposes the bare model ID. The legacy provider/model form keeps working as a routing alias. Two providers may expose the same name on purpose: the gateway pools them.

template.description: Provider template this entry was created from (provenance only; it does not affect routing).

quota.description: Subscription usage mapping. The gateway queries each credential's own plan endpoint and the UI shows the resulting windows as quota cards. Use a built-in preset, spell the mapping out inline, or mix both (inline values win).

preset.description: Built-in usage mapping id (see the server's quota presets, e.g. opencode-go).

endpoint.description: Absolute URL polled for usage data, or a "{base}/path" template resolved against the provider's own endpoint (self-hosted aggregators such as new-api and sub2api). Required unless a preset supplies it.

script.description: JavaScript expression that produces the usage snapshot instead of endpoint/windows/extras. Two shapes: CC Switch compatible ({request: {url, method, headers, body}, extractor: (response) => ...}) where {{baseUrl}}/{{apiKey}} are substituted in the request fields, or an async function (ctx) => ({windows, extras}) with a synchronous ctx.fetch. See docs/quota-scripts.md. Do not hardcode credentials: use {{apiKey}} or ctx.apiKey.

style.description: How the credential is presented: Authorization: Bearer (default), a custom header, or nothing.

header.description: Header name used when style is "header".

headers.description: Extra request headers for the quota request.

refreshInterval.description: Background refresh cadence (Go duration, minimum 30s). Empty means manual refresh only; enabling enforce without an interval defaults to 5m.

windows.description: Usage windows shown in order, each mapped out of the response with a gjson path.

id.description: Window identifier (rolling, weekly, monthly, ...). Known ids get a localized label; others use label.

label.description: Display fallback when the id has no translation.

path.description: gjson path to the window object, e.g. usage.rolling.

percent.description: Field (relative to path) holding the percentage. With limit set it names the USED amount instead, and the share is computed as used/limit.

percentMode.description: Whether the percentage is the used share (default) or the remaining share. Not applicable to amount windows (see limit).

limit.description: Field (relative to path) holding the window's total allowance. Aggregators (new-api, sub2api) publish absolute used/limit counters: with limit set, percent names the used amount and the used share becomes used/limit*100. A zero limit renders as "unlimited".

status.description: Optional field holding a status string, e.g. ok / rate-limited.

resetsAt.description: Optional field holding the window reset timestamp (RFC3339).

optional.description: Mark a window some responses legitimately omit (a relay reports either a subscription window or a wallet balance). An absent optional window is dropped instead of flagged as a broken mapping.

extras.description: Additional scalar rows shown next to the windows (credit balance, counters, ...). An extra whose path is absent is skipped, so one mapping can cover several response modes.

divideBy.description: Divides a numeric value before display (0 = keep it). Aggregators count quota in internal units: new-api defaults to 500000 per USD.

suffix.description: Appended to the rendered value, e.g. " USD".

format.description: Convert a timestamp to RFC3339. A zero timestamp means "never" and is omitted.

divideBy.description: Default divisor for every numeric extra and window amount in this mapping (0 = keep raw values). A per-extra divideBy wins.

enforce.description: Optionally park a credential whose usage window is full. Disabled by default: quota is observability unless enabled here.

threshold.description: Used percentage at or above which the credential is parked.

fallbackCooldown.description: Park duration used when the full window carries no reset timestamp.

value.description: The API key value. Omitted from config JSON output.

valueEnv.description: Environment variable holding the API key value. Used when value is empty.

weight.description: Weighted-round-robin weight. Defaults to the provider weight.

priority.description: Priority tier. Defaults to the provider priority.

maxConcurrent.description: Per-key concurrent request cap. 0 means unlimited.

apiKeys.description: Upstream API keys. Keys are scheduled by priority tier with weighted round-robin inside each tier.

oneOf.description: Shorthand mapping: the key is the local model ID, the value is the upstream model name.

local.description: Model ID exposed by the gateway.

remote.description: Upstream model name sent to the provider. Defaults to local.

pricing.description: Pin the pricing-catalog entry used to estimate this model's cost. Empty parts resolve from the provider (its pricingProvider, else its own id lowercased) and the upstream model name.

provider.description: Provider id in the pricing catalog.

model.description: Model name in the pricing catalog.

models.description: Models served by this provider. A string maps the model to itself; an object maps a local gateway model ID to an upstream model name.

responseHeader.description: Time to wait for response headers in seconds.

timeouts.description: Timeout settings for connections to this provider.

pricingProvider.description: Pricing-catalog provider id for this provider's models. Empty falls back to the provider's own id, lowercased.

providers.description: A dictionary of upstream LLM providers. The gateway forwards matching requests to the provider's API, scheduling between multiple API keys per provider (priority tiers, weighted round-robin, cooldowns) with optional per-provider or per-key outbound proxies.

stickyTTL.description: Idle expiry for provider session-affinity entries. A hit slides the expiry forward (Go duration, e.g. 30m, 1h). Affinity is scoped to one conversation and one model.

failover.description: Which upstream responses make the gateway continue on another credential (or another provider serving the same bare model name) before the client sees the error.

crossProvider.description: Allow one request to continue on another provider that serves the same bare model name. A provider-qualified name (provider/model) always stays pinned to that provider.

statuses.description: Replace the default failover set (every 3xx/4xx/5xx except 413). Example: [429, 500, 502, 503].

excludeStatuses.description: Remove statuses from the effective set, e.g. [400, 413] to hand client-input errors straight back.

skipSlow.description: Prefer the provider that answers fastest: a provider whose measured first-token latency is far worse than the alternatives serving the same model is passed over. The measurements are taken from this deployment's own traffic, so the rule adapts to the workload. Skipping only happens when another candidate is available and trusted, so a lone provider, a cold start and a reload are never affected.

enabled.description: Turn the behaviour off to keep every provider a candidate regardless of latency.

maxFirstTokenMs.description: Skip a provider whose smoothed first-token latency exceeds this many milliseconds. 0 (default) leaves this rule off, since the right ceiling depends on the model.

relativeFactor.description: Skip a provider slower than the fastest candidate by this multiple (default 3). A factor rather than a difference, so 2s vs 6s and 5s vs 15s count the same.

minSamples.description: How many measurements a provider needs before its latency is trusted (default 3). Fewer samples always fail open, so a cold start or one slow request cannot drop a provider.

probeInterval.description: How long a skipped provider stays out of the pool before it is admitted again for one measurement (default 5m, "0s" disables probing). Skipping is self-reinforcing: a provider that is never picked produces no new measurement, so its smoothed latency freezes at the value that excluded it and a recovered provider could never prove it. Without probing one slow period removes a provider for good.

auth.description: Cooldown applied to a key after a 401/402 response (Go duration). The first 401 only benches for authProbe so a transient upstream hiccup self-heals; a repeated 401 within two minutes escalates to this value. 402 keeps the full cooldown immediately, and a 403 is treated as a model/region policy rejection: it fails over without benching the key.

authProbe.description: How long the FIRST 401 benches a key (Go duration). Set to 0s to disable probing: every 401 gets the full auth cooldown.

rateLimit.description: Cooldown applied to a key after a 429 without a usable Retry-After header (Go duration).

transient.description: Cooldown applied to a key after 5xx or network errors (Go duration).

cooldown.description: Cooldown durations per upstream error class.

emptyResponse.description: Retry a success response that carries no model output. A provider occasionally answers 200 and then produces nothing (a lifecycle-only stream, an empty choices array, a truncated tool call); nothing has reached the client at that point, so the request continues on the next credential or provider instead of delivering an empty success downstream.

retry.description: Retry a success response that carries no model output (default true).

hold.description: How long a streaming response may be inspected before its first content (Go duration, e.g. 15s). After the hold the response is committed and streamed unchanged, so a slow provider is not mistaken for a broken one. 0 disables stream inspection; whole-body responses are still checked.

gateway.description: Gateway-wide settings for upstream provider forwarding.

upstream.description: Controls behaviour of the /upstream passthrough endpoint. Recommended to only use in special use cases; leaving it as the default will typically be the best experience.

ignorePaths.description: List of RE2 compatible regular expressions. Any request to a path matching any of the regular expressions will be ignored and not trigger a swap. When not specified, defaults to a pattern matching common static-asset suffixes (.js, .json, .css, .png, .gif, .jpg, .jpeg, .ico, .txt).

routing.description: Canonical routing/scheduling configuration. Alternative to the legacy top-level 'groups'/'matrix' keys; a config must not use both styles.

scheduler.description: Scheduler configuration. Decides the order in which queued requests are serviced.

use.description: Scheduler to use. Only 'fifo' is currently supported.

priority.description: Per-model priority. Keys are model IDs, values are integers (default 0). Higher values are serviced first.

router.description: Router configuration. Selects between the group and matrix swapping strategies.

use.description: Router to use. 'group' uses static groups, 'matrix' uses the solver-based swap matrix.

extensions.description: Programmable request, response and tool extensions. Disabled by default.

resourceBudget.description: Budget of host resources llama-swap may give to managed runtimes and containers.

vramMiB.description: Total VRAM managed runtimes may occupy, in MiB. 0 means no limit.

ramMiB.description: Total system memory managed runtimes may occupy, in MiB. 0 means no limit.

autoEvict.description: Stop the least recently used runtime when the budget is exceeded instead of failing the start.

queueLoads.description: Queue model loads when the runtime is busy instead of rejecting the load.

network.description: Outbound proxy policy for every host-side client and child process: model downloads, pricing refresh, runtime metadata, extension fetches, provider fallbacks, and the package managers runtime builds run. The section also decides which address counts as the caller for API-key IP allowlists and audit rows.

proxy.description: Proxy URL: http(s)://, socks5:// or socks5h:// (credentials allowed). 'direct' or 'none' forces direct connections, ignoring the process environment. Empty follows HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY/ALL_PROXY/NO_PROXY.

noProxy.description: Hosts that bypass the proxy. An exact host or a leading-dot domain suffix matches that domain and its subdomains; '*' disables proxying entirely.

trustForwardedFor.description: Trust X-Forwarded-For / X-Real-IP when resolving the caller address. Enable only when every request arrives through a reverse proxy you control: a direct client could otherwise claim any address and defeat the per-key allowedIps allowlist. When false (the default) the TCP peer address is always used.

trustedProxies.description: Peer addresses or CIDR blocks allowed to supply forwarding headers (for example 127.0.0.1/32 or 10.0.0.0/8). Requires trustForwardedFor: true. Empty means any peer, which is only safe when the listener is reachable solely through the proxy.

rollbackOnModelStartFailure.description: What happens when a model fails to start with a newly applied configuration. true (the default) restores the last configuration that started so the model keeps serving. false keeps the new configuration and takes the model out of service: it refuses to be started by incoming requests until a later start succeeds and serves a request.

runtimes.description: Managed runtime definitions. One key per runtime; a model's backend.runtime points at one of them.

kind.description: What this runtime provides. Omitted means llamacpp.

mode.description: native installs into a versioned directory; container runs it in a container.

source.description: Where the runtime comes from. Exactly one source type is meaningful per definition.

repository.description: Source repository, as owner/name for a GitHub source.

asset.description: GitHub Release asset name template for a native release channel. {tag} and {version} expand.

trackRef.description: Ref whose tag list is followed when tracking releases.

ref.description: Branch, tag or commit ref for a git source.

url.description: Direct download URL for a wheel or archive.

path.description: Absolute path to a local source tree or install root.

image.description: Container image reference for a container-mode runtime.

platform.description: Container platform override, for example linux/arm64.

checksum.description: Expected SHA-256 of the downloaded artifact. Verified before installation.

build.description: How to build the runtime when the source is not a prebuilt artifact.

backend.description: Backend flavour passed to the build.

compiler.description: C/C++ compiler for cmake and make drivers.

cudaArchitectures.description: CUDA architectures to build for, for example 70;7.5.

python.description: Interpreter selector for the uv driver.

indexURL.description: Package index for the uv driver.

steps.description: Explicit build steps for the custom driver. No shell is involved.

from.description: Path inside the staged build directory.

artifacts.description: Build outputs copied into the installed version.

container.description: Container settings for a container-mode runtime.

stopTimeout.description: Grace period before SIGKILL, in seconds or as a duration such as 10s.

update.description: Update policy for a tracked runtime.

version.description: Exact version to pin. Requires policy: pinned.

checkEvery.description: How often to look for a new version, as seconds or a duration such as 6h.

minIdle.description: How long the runtime must be idle before an update is applied.

verify.description: Checks run against a freshly installed runtime before it is activated.

sha256.description: Expected digest of the installed runtime.

healthPath.description: Path probed during a readiness check.

smokeCommand.description: Command that must exit 0 to accept the version.

metadata.description: Runtime launch metadata every model on this runtime inherits: the launch head for runtimes that front a custom server, and the quick-config engine defaults. A model overrides any of them — its own entrypoint wins, and a flag written in its args beats the corresponding default.

entrypoint.description: Launch head for models on this runtime, for example "python3 /scripts/server.py". Runs verbatim followed by the model's args; no engine flags, host or port are injected. Empty keeps the kind's canonical entrypoint.

contextPerRequest.description: Default per-request context (--max-model-len / --ctx-size) for models that do not pin it.

maxConcurrency.description: Default concurrency (--max-num-seqs / --parallel) for models that do not pin it.

tensorParallelSize.description: Default tensor parallel size for vLLM models that do not pin it.

gpuMemoryUtilization.description: Default GPU memory utilization (0-1) for vLLM models that do not pin it.

server.description: HTTP accept-loop limits and defensive response headers. Timeouts that would cut a streaming response are intentionally absent.

maxHeaderBytes.description: Upper bound on the request line plus headers. Defaults to 64 KiB, well below Go's 1 MiB default.

readTimeout.description: Bounds reading one complete request. 0 disables it so a large payload on a slow link is not cut off.

securityHeaders.description: Emit X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy and, for the UI, a Content-Security-Policy. Set false only when a fronting proxy already supplies them.

authRateLimit.description: Throttle failed credential checks per caller address. A success clears the counter.

maxFailures.description: Failed checks allowed inside window before blockFor starts.

window.description: Sliding window the failures are counted over.

blockFor.description: How long a caller is rejected once the limit is reached.

cors.description: Access-Control-* headers for browser clients. Leaving allowedOrigins out selects the permissive legacy policy (any origin); setting it means only the listed origins may read responses. The cross-origin management-write guard on /api/ is independent of this block.

allowedOrigins.description: Browser origins allowed to read responses, as scheme://host[:port]. "*" allows any origin and cannot be combined with allowCredentials or allowPrivateNetwork. An absent key keeps the permissive default; an empty list is rejected.

allowCredentials.description: Send Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true so the browser attaches cookies and Authorization headers.

allowPrivateNetwork.description: Answer Chrome's Private Network Access preflight (Access-Control-Allow-Private-Network). Cannot be combined with a "*" origin.

allowedMethods.description: Methods advertised on preflight responses. Empty means GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, OPTIONS.

allowedHeaders.description: Header names advertised on preflight responses. Empty echoes the client's sanitized Access-Control-Request-Headers.

exposedHeaders.description: Response headers a browser may read beyond the CORS-safelisted set.

pricing.description: Cost estimation for the usage records page. The models.dev catalog is synchronized automatically; explicit per-model pricing refs and operator-edited catalog rows always win over the snapshot.

ambiguity.description: How a model name priced by several catalog providers is resolved: a lone operator-edited row wins first, then the official vendor's entry, then the serving provider's entry, then the only non-zero one; strict stops before those guesses, lowest falls back to the cheapest remaining entry. Default provider-first.

vendors.description: Model-name prefix -> pricing-catalog provider id treated as the model's official vendor ("gemini" -> "google"). Merged over the built-in table, which covers: gpt/o1/o3/o4->openai, gemini->google, qwen/qvq/qwq->alibaba, glm->zhipuai, deepseek->deepseek, claude->anthropic, kimi->moonshotai, minimax->minimax, grok->xai, mimo->xiaomi, step->stepfun, mistral/ministral/codestral/devstral/magistral/pixtral/voxtral->mistral, doubao->volcengine, command->cohere, sonar->perplexity, muse->meta, phi->azure, nvidia->nvidia.

costBackfillOnSync.description: After each successful catalog sync, recompute the cost of activity rows recorded before their model had a price, using the current catalog, and persist it (default true). Already-priced rows are never recomputed.
